clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke and death in June 1991, within eighteen months: your wrist injury stopped your playing that October, you and Rafe clashed and he moved out within weeks, you were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios, then lost and low unable to get going by early 1992 with anxiety up and functioning down. Your mother's thyroid surgery sat nearby in those same months. Your symptom of late nights had been climbing since you were at secondary school; it rose again through this time. By the spring of 1992 when you earned money fixing radios and by autumn when you went to the community college, the acute crisis had passed, though the bleak year at college followed close after.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, within two and a half years: you were running out of steam for performing with anxiety up and functioning down, then had a disastrous audition and were done with performing, on poor terms with family and friends. You left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol and moved to Fenwick with her within months, then split from her and sank into a deep depression once back in Thornbury that winter. You could not face your family but relied, gingerly, on friends. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home in the autumn of 2003; she died in February 2004. The period settles as you began swimming laps, requested help from your parents with therapy costs, and returned to your therapist, with functioning beginning to rise.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within seven months: you were too drained for conversation when building at Alder Creek in July, your mother pressed to visit you against your wishes and the visit went wrong, then you left for nursing school in September and stopped speaking to her; the silence held for roughly a year. By the autumn you had settled into the nursing programme and the relationship distance, though it remained, had become a structured cutoff rather than an acute rupture.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two and a half years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your anxiety about always driving projects forward was constant by October 2019, you started a sleeping pill though sleep itself did not improve. When Wren's family gathered for her mother's retirement party in late October 2019, Wren was swamped one thing after another with symptom and anxiety up and functioning down, you overfunctioned too strictly laying out a plan to settle her, Wren's family fused tightly talking all day with nothing happening to one the others did not hear, then Wren settled once the weekend had a plan. At the lake house you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep, could only pull back as others rose, symptom and anxiety up and distance from the group; Wren grew anxious when you had had no sleep at family occasions. Your cousin Bella was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your sister Tara had a baby on the way in October 2019, and by then your cousin Leo had returned to live nearby. The period settles as you aimed for shorter, more regular calls with your mother to soften the distance that piles up.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
